source.title: Global Bidirectional DC/DC Power Converter Market to Reach USD 61.85 Million by 2034, Driven by Battery Storage and Electric Mobility Applications
source.body:
PUNE, India, November 23, 2026 – The global bidirectional DC/DC power converter market is projected to reach USD 61.85 million by 2034, expanding at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 24.8% during 2026–2034, according to a new report published by EnergyResourcesInsights. The market was valued at USD 8.41 million in 2025 and is estimated to reach USD 10.50 million in 2026.
The report, titled “Bidirectional DC/DC Power Converter Market – Size, Share & Industry Analysis, By Electrical Architecture, By Application, By Rated Output Power, By Packaging, and Global Forecast, 2026–2034,” examines specialized power-conversion equipment that transfers electrical energy in both directions between different direct-current (DC) voltage levels. These converters are used to connect battery storage systems with DC buses, support electric mobility and charging infrastructure, integrate renewable energy systems and recover energy in industrial equipment.
Unlike conventional one-way converters, bidirectional DC/DC systems support both charging and discharging operations through a controlled power stage. This capability enables batteries to exchange energy with different voltage networks, supports flexible DC distribution and can simplify power architectures by reducing the need for separate charging and discharging paths.
Growing deployment of battery energy storage, DC-coupled charging equipment, renewable-energy integration and regenerative industrial systems is creating opportunities for specialized bidirectional converter modules. At the same time, product qualification, thermal management, electromagnetic compatibility and integration requirements remain important considerations for manufacturers and buyers.
Bidirectional DC/DC Power Converter Market at a Glance
•	2025 Market Size: USD 8.41 Million
•	2026 Market Estimate: USD 10.50 Million
•	2034 Market Forecast: USD 61.85 Million
•	CAGR (2026–2034): 24.8%
•	Largest Regional Market: Asia-Pacific
•	Report ID: #397
•	Report Length: 81 Pages
•	Publication: November 2026
Key Factors Driving the Bidirectional DC/DC Power Converter Market
1. Expansion of DC-Coupled Battery Storage Systems
The growing deployment of stationary battery energy storage systems is supporting demand for bidirectional DC/DC converters. These devices connect battery strings to DC buses operating at different voltage levels and regulate power during charging and discharging. Their ability to manage changing battery voltage and controlled reverse energy flow makes them relevant to storage architectures requiring flexible DC interfaces.
2. Increasing Bidirectional Interfaces in EV Charging and Electric Mobility
Electric mobility applications increasingly require power conversion between different DC voltage domains. Bidirectional DC/DC converters can support charging equipment, vehicle auxiliary networks and energy-transfer systems. Their role in DC-bus charging infrastructure and battery interfaces is creating opportunities for specialized converter suppliers.
3. Adoption of High-Efficiency Silicon-Carbide and Soft-Switching Designs
Power-electronics manufacturers are exploring silicon-carbide (SiC) devices and advanced switching topologies to improve conversion efficiency and power density. Isolated dual-active-bridge and resonant converter designs are relevant to applications involving substantial voltage differences, while synchronous buck-boost and fixed-ratio converters support selected non-isolated applications.
4. Industrial Regeneration and DC Microgrid Integration
Industrial equipment such as cranes, lifts and automated machinery can recover energy during braking and deceleration. Bidirectional DC/DC converters can transfer recovered energy to storage systems or other DC loads. DC microgrids also use reversible conversion stages to manage energy exchange between batteries, renewable generation and connected loads.
5. Standardization of Power Modules and Equipment Upgrades
OEMs and system integrators are increasingly evaluating standardized converter modules that can be deployed across multiple equipment platforms. Modular designs can reduce custom engineering requirements and simplify integration. Product reliability, communication interfaces, protection behaviour, thermal performance and documented qualification remain essential purchasing criteria.
Market Segmentation
The Bidirectional DC/DC Power Converter Market is segmented across four major categories:
•	By Electrical Architecture: Isolated DC/DC Converter, Non-isolated DC/DC Converter.
•	By Application: Battery Energy Storage, Electric Mobility and Charging, DC Microgrids and Renewables, Industrial and Test Equipment.
•	By Rated Output Power: 5 kW and Below, Above 5 kW to 20 kW, Above 20 kW.
•	By Packaging: Power Modules and Board Assemblies, Enclosed and Rackmount Units.
Isolated DC/DC converters represented an estimated 60% of global revenue in 2025, making them the leading electrical architecture category. Battery energy storage was the largest application segment, accounting for an estimated 40% of converter hardware revenue.
Converters rated above 20 kW represented an estimated 40% of market revenue, reflecting the importance of higher-value power modules. Power modules and board assemblies accounted for an estimated 67% of global converter sales by packaging, supported by demand from OEMs and system integrators seeking embedded conversion solutions.
These segment shares are analytical estimates presented in the report and refer to standalone bidirectional DC/DC converter hardware revenue.
Regional Outlook
Asia-Pacific is the largest regional market, accounting for an estimated 46% of global revenue in 2025. The region benefits from power-electronics manufacturing capabilities, battery storage development, electric vehicle charging infrastructure and industrial DC power applications. China is a major production and demand centre, with suppliers such as Tonhe Technology and Infypower offering bidirectional DC/DC converter products. Japan also contributes through specialized power-conversion equipment, including TDK's EZA converter series. India, South Korea, Australia and Southeast Asia represent additional opportunities linked to solar generation, commercial battery systems and electric mobility.
Europe accounted for an estimated 24% of global revenue in 2025. Demand is supported by energy-storage infrastructure, industrial electrification, automated material handling and regenerative industrial applications. Germany and other established industrial markets place emphasis on converter reliability, electrical safety documentation, serviceability and product qualification.
North America represented an estimated 22% of global demand in 2025, supported by power-module development, distributed storage and vehicle-electronics engineering. The United States is an important centre for power-conversion design, with companies such as Vicor supplying bidirectional DC bus modules. Engineering platforms and reference designs from Texas Instruments and Analog Devices also contribute to the broader converter technology ecosystem.
South America is an emerging market, with opportunities in battery storage, photovoltaic integration, mining electrification and industrial power systems. Brazil and Chile are among the markets evaluating applications for reversible DC power conversion. Imported equipment costs, technical support and project financing remain important considerations.
The Middle East & Africa market remains smaller and selective, with opportunities in utility storage, remote energy systems, telecommunications infrastructure and industrial power applications. High ambient temperatures, dust exposure, equipment protection and access to maintenance services influence product selection.
Regional revenue shares are analytical estimates provided by the report.
Competitive Landscape
The global bidirectional DC/DC power converter market includes specialist power-module manufacturers and suppliers of enclosed converter equipment. The report identifies the following key companies:
•	Vicor
•	Infypower
•	Tonhe Technology
•	TDK
Vicor offers bidirectional fixed-ratio DC bus modules, while Infypower supplies bidirectional DC/DC products within its charging and energy-storage equipment portfolio. Tonhe Technology offers isolated bidirectional DC/DC modules for charging DC buses and microgrid storage. TDK markets EZA-series isolated bidirectional converters for energy storage and industrial energy-recovery applications.
The wider technology ecosystem also includes semiconductor and engineering-platform companies such as Texas Instruments, Analog Devices and Wolfspeed. These companies provide controllers, power semiconductors and reference designs that support converter development, although they are not automatically classified as suppliers of finished merchant converter modules.
Competition is shaped by conversion efficiency, power density, isolation capability, voltage range, thermal management, electromagnetic compatibility, fault protection and integration flexibility. Manufacturers also need to demonstrate reliable operation in both power-flow directions and provide clear technical documentation to support OEM qualification.
